title: Karna: the wheel stuck, the death
hook: Karna takes command, and asks for a king to hold his reins
tomorrow: Karna: the wheel stuck, the death

segments.voice: Yesterday: Drona, the teacher, fell, and your line was the ground itself took note. Bhishma is down, and now Drona too. So who leads the Kauravas now?

A new commander needs a driver. In the Kaurava camp, Duryodhana turns to his friend Karna and gives him the army. Karna accepts, and then he says something honest. Arjuna has an advantage I don't, he tells Duryodhana, in effect: he has Krishna holding his reins. If I'm to face him, I need a charioteer who knows horses the way Krishna does. And Karna names the man: Shalya, king of Madra, the uncle of the Pandava twins, who ended up fighting on the Kaurava side.
screen: `KARNA TAKES COMMAND.` → `ARJUNA HAS KRISHNA.` → `I NEED SHALYA.`

segments.voice: Duryodhana goes to Shalya and asks, and Shalya is furious. In Ganguli's English, the king takes it as an insult: he, a crowned king, told to drive for Karna, who was raised in a charioteer's house. He nearly walks out of the camp. So Duryodhana talks him round. He praises Shalya's skill with horses, calls him Krishna's equal at the reins, and tells an old story of the gods in which the creator Brahma himself drove the chariot for Shiva. Driving, in that story, is no shame. Shalya agrees, with one condition: he'll say whatever he likes to Karna's face. Karna accepts. Now the layer underneath. Before the war began, the epic tells us, Shalya met Yudhishthira and made him a promise. If he ever drove for Karna against Arjuna, he would wear down Karna's courage with his words. So the man stepping into Karna's chariot carries a promise to the other side. Karna asked for a driver to match Krishna, and he got one. He also got a voice in his ear that was never quite his. The story doesn't hurry to tell us how that will go. It just lets the two men climb into the same chariot.
screen: `KARNA ASKS FOR SHALYA` · `A KING TOLD TO DRIVE` · `I WILL SAY WHAT I LIKE` · then, large: `A PROMISE TO THE OTHER SIDE`

segments.voice: Rest your hands on your knees, loosely, like reins held without pulling, and breathe slowly. Notice the voices riding along with you today, in your head and beside you, and whose is nearest the reins. You don't have to answer any of them; if you pray, you can rest in prayer here.
Karna. The new commander of the Kauravas, who asks for a king to drive him, and gets a king who carries a promise to the other side.
Your line: a voice in his ear. Shalya took the reins with a promise already made. Day eight hundred thirty-seven, done.

howItsDone: Hindus meet Karna's last battle through recitations and readings of the Mahabharata, retellings, regional theater and television serials; the Karna Parva, the epic's book named for him, tells this part of the war.

original.note: charioteer: what Krishna is for Arjuna, and what Karna asks Shalya to be.

trapdoor: what you thought: a charioteer just drives the horses.
what it means: in the epic the charioteer rides close enough to advise, warn and steady the warrior, as Krishna does for Arjuna.
what a scholar hears: Karna was raised in a charioteer's house, so his request turns an old insult around: now a king must do the work Karna was mocked for.
recall: the minister who built a house to burn

chat.says: Why did Karna ask for Shalya, of all people, to drive his chariot?
options: He wanted a charioteer who knew horses the way Krishna does for Arjuna.
Shalya asked for the job so he could keep his nephews safe in battle.
Shalya was the only king left in the camp who had ever driven a chariot.
chat.meaning: Arjuna had Krishna at his reins. Karna asked for Shalya to match him, not knowing Shalya's promise to Yudhishthira.

Shalya.meaning: king of Madra, uncle of the Pandava twins

Shiva.meaning: the great god for whom Brahma drove, in Duryodhana's story

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Karna Parva, Karna made commander and his request for Shalya as charioteer; Shalya's anger, Duryodhana's persuasion (including the story of Brahma driving Shiva's chariot) and Shalya's condition
Mahabharata, Udyoga Parva, Shalya's promise to Yudhishthira to dishearten Karna
